BiblicalUsage: Saul spares the best of the spoil and destroys only what is vile and despised, keeping the good and throwing away the worthless — and the LORD rejects him for it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Saul's bargain is the picture of half-obedience: he keeps the best and destroys the refuse, and calls it sacrifice, but God calls it rebellion.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
